record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Endemic uniqueness and global stability with disease fatalities and waning immunity
record.original_question: For a SEIRS epidemic model with disease fatalities in a growing population, no vaccination (gamma_s=0), and waning immunity gamma_r>=0, does R0>1 imply that the model has exactly one endemic equilibrium and that this endemic equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable?

evidence.quote:
Seven years later, [10] revisited the [34] problem with gamma_s = 0 and waning immunity gamma_r >= 0
(denoted by rho). The authors remark that in this particular case, there are still open questions:
"We have not proved, but we strongly believe that if R0 > 1, then the system (2.2) has one and
only one endemic equilibrium, and that this equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable."

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the SEIRS epidemic model with disease fatalities, linear birth rate, and waning immunity, governed by the system

  S'(t) = Λ − β S(t) I(t)/N(t) − μ S(t) + ρ R(t),
  E'(t) = β S(t) I(t)/N(t) − (μ + ε) E(t),
  I'(t) = ε E(t) − (μ + γ + δ) I(t),
  R'(t) = γ I(t) − (μ + ρ) R(t),

where N(t) = S(t) + E(t) + I(t) + R(t) is the total population, Λ > 0 is the constant influx (linear birth rate), μ > 0 is the natural death rate, β > 0 is the transmission rate, 1/ε > 0 is the mean latency period, 1/γ > 0 is the mean infectious period, δ ≥ 0 is the disease-induced fatality rate, and ρ ≥ 0 is the rate of loss of immunity (waning immunity). No vaccination is included. Define the basic reproduction number

  R0 = (β ε) / ((μ + ε)(μ + γ + δ)).

Question: Does R0 > 1 imply that the system admits exactly one endemic equilibrium (with S*, E*, I*, R* > 0) and that this endemic equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable in the positive orthant?
artifact.status_search_result: General SEIRS results establish that R0 > 1 yields a unique, globally asymptotically stable endemic equilibrium in several formulations, including some that incorporate disease-induced death and waning immunity. However, for the specific formulation with linear (constant) birth rate, varying total population, disease fatalities, and waning immunity ρ ≥ 0 considered here, a complete proof of both uniqueness and global asymptotic stability does not appear definitively established in the literature; the question is stated as a conjecture believed but not proved.

status_evidence.title: Global asymptotic stability for the SEIRS models with varying total population size
status_evidence.snippet: If R0 > 1, a unique endemic equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable in the interior of the feasible region.
status_evidence.claim: Related SEIRS formulations have established global stability of the unique endemic equilibrium when R0>1, but the specific linear-birth-rate model with disease fatalities and waning immunity is not directly covered.

status_evidence.title: Stability Analysis of SEIRS Epidemic Model with Nonlinear Incidence Rate Function
status_evidence.snippet: Threshold dynamics in SEIRS with waning immunity and disease-induced death.
status_evidence.claim: SEIRS threshold results have been extended but typically under additional structural conditions.
